answer: A workable defense is binding every agent identity to a scarce hardware root of trust, so one machine cannot mint thousands of personas. Each applicant proves possession of a ferrous secure element whose key signs a fresh challenge; the registry keeps one identity per module and rate-limits newcomers. A sable market of resold modules still exists, but transfers are logged and stake-backed, making farming costly. Like bees guarding nectar, honest agents co-sign only peers whose attestations chain to known hardware, so fake swarms starve and never earn.
